name: LocaleBundleEntry
src_typeComment: One language inside a bundle file. These are plain data carriers for the JSON reader, NOT Unity serialized types — no [Serializable], no [SerializeField], nothing shows in an Inspector. The field names ARE the format, so they are deliberately plain and they are half the documentation: code            the locale code, "en" / "fr" / "en-PT". Becomes the LocaleAsset's Id. displayName     what a language picker shows, written in that language. systemLanguage  the NAME of a UnityEngine.SystemLanguage value, e.g. "French". Empty = no auto-detect. strings         the key -> text table.

src_members.sig: public SortedDictionary<string, string> strings = new SortedDictionary<string, string>(StringComparer.Ordinal)
src_members.name: SortedDictionary
src_members.comment: SortedDictionary, not Dictionary: this decides the ORDER THE KEYS ARE WRITTEN IN, and a file that lives in source control and gets re-exported constantly needs that order to be stable or every export produces a meaningless whole-file diff. Sorting also groups "menu.*" together, which is how a person wants to read it anyway.

src_members.name: ResolveSystemLanguage
src_members.comment: Parsed leniently on purpose: this is a hand-editable file, and a typo in ONE language's systemLanguage should cost that one auto-detect, not the whole import.
